_comment: Lens assignment for deslop swarm passes. Every per-principle file under references/<category>/ must appear in exactly one lens; scripts/swarm_lenses.py --check enforces that and refuses to emit prompts otherwise. Grouping logic: a lens is a single reading stance — the principles in it are the ones whose findings a reader must weigh against each other (boundary ownership vs boundary parsing vs shape vs legibility). Related principles deliberately live together so a swarmed pass does not report the same smell twice under two names.

boundaries.stance: Where does this code belong, and does each part hold one concern? Judge seams, ownership and cohesion — not function size.

duplication.stance: What knowledge exists more than once, and where is its single owner? Read duplication.md as well — the sweep primitives live there.

coupling.stance: What does each unit know about its neighbours, and what does it construct or reach through that it should have been handed?

parsing.stance: Where does an external value enter, and which single component turns it into a decision? Follow each input from the edge to every place that re-interprets it.

shape.stance: How big and how tangled is each unit's control flow? Depth, conditional chains, parameter lists, nesting — the measurable shape of the code.

legibility.stance: Can a competent stranger read this without the author present? Naming, comment discipline, surprise, elegance, and code that copes where it should decide.

guarantees.stance: What does this code promise, who claims the promise, and what happens when it is broken? State, lifetime, cancellation, privilege, and telling the truth when it fails.

data-layer.stance: If there is a database: what does the schema promise, what does the query shape do to it, and where is an invariant only in application code?
data-layer.skip_when: the target has no schema, migration, ORM model or SQL — say so in the report rather than inventing findings
